details: On November 24, 2026, the European Central Bank (ECB) published its Tokenisation Reference Model (TRM) to guide the standardization of Europe's tokenized financial ecosystem. This framework aims to foster common standards and prevent fragmentation in Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT)-based markets, focusing on legal, governance, semantic, operational, and infrastructural domains. It emphasizes key capabilities such as interoperability, transferability, portability, controllability, and composability for tokenized assets, signaling a structured approach to integrating DLT into traditional finance.
title: ECB Proposes Framework for DLT Standardisation in Europe

details: Bitcoin experienced a drop of over 2% on November 25, 2026, falling below the $60,000 mark. This decline is attributed to increased risk aversion among investors ahead of the crucial US October Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index release. Market expectations for core PCE to rise 0.3% month-over-month, potentially reaching 3.8% year-over-year (above the Federal Reserve's 2% target), are fueling predictions of a 25-basis-point Fed rate hike in December (with a 96% probability) and further monetary tightening in early 2027.
title: Bitcoin Falls on PCE Inflation Concerns, $50,000 Test Looms

details: The European Central Bank's November 2026 Financial Stability Review highlighted elevated risks to financial stability stemming from ambitious Artificial Intelligence (AI) valuations, fiscal imbalances across major economies, and persistent geoeconomic tensions. Separately, the ECB proposed revising the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCAR) to replace minimum deposit requirements for stablecoin issuers with more flexible, liquidity-based criteria for reserve assets.
title: ECB Warns of AI Risks in Finance, Seeks Flexible Stablecoin Rules

details: Kristalina Georgieva, Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), warned that the surging demand for AI hardware and infrastructure, coupled with the ongoing energy shock from the Middle East conflict, is projected to push global inflation to 4.7% in 2026. This combined inflationary pressure is expected to necessitate tighter monetary policies and potentially higher interest rates from central banks worldwide.
title: IMF: AI Demand and Energy Shock to Boost Global Inflation, Rates

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) emphasized that the increasing use of weakly backed US dollar stablecoins in emerging markets poses significant risks to global financial stability. The IMF report outlines concerns including potential for currency substitution, instability in capital flows, and challenges to the effectiveness of monetary policy and fiscal integrity in these economies, especially during periods of financial stress or large-scale redemptions.
title: IMF Warns on Stablecoin Risks to Emerging Market Financial Stability
